title: Finite generic fibers become a finite morphism near the generic points
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism] which is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $Y$ be Noetherian (locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact). Suppose the set-theoretic fiber $f^{-1}(\{\eta\})$ is finite for every generic point $\eta$ [def-sc-generic-point] of every irreducible component [def-weil-irreducible-components] of $Y$. Then there exists a dense open subscheme $V\subseteq Y$ containing all these generic points such that $f^{-1}(V)\to V$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism].

source.place: Tag 02NW, label lemma-generically-finite, equivalence (1) and (4), at the finitely many generic points

proof.text: Fix a generic point $\eta$ of a component of $Y$ and choose an affine neighbourhood $V_0=\operatorname{Spec}R$. Put $X_0=f^{-1}(V_0)$ and $f_0:X_0\to V_0$. The open-fibre-product identification and quasi-compact base change make $f_0$ quasi-compact; also $X_0$ is quasi-compact by the definition. To check $X_0$ quasi-separated directly, take affine opens $A,B\subseteq X_0$. The open-fibre-product lemma identifies $A\times_{V_0}B$ with an open of $X\times_YX$, and the affine tensor-product lemma makes it affine, hence quasi-compact. Its preimage under the quasi-compact diagonal of $f$ is $A\cap B$, hence quasi-compact. The affine-cover criterion now proves $X_0$ quasi-separated. The intersection of the component of $\eta$ with $V_0$ is a component of $V_0$: any irreducible subset containing it has closure in $Y$ containing the original component, hence equals that component. Thus $\eta$ is still generic in $V_0$.

Write $f^{-1}(\{\eta\})=\{\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_n\}$. The finite-fibre lemma gives a discrete scheme fibre, and the fibre homeomorphism gives no nontrivial specializations among the $\xi_i$. For any generalization $x$ of $\xi_i$ in $X_0$, $f(x)$ is a generalization of $\eta$. There is no proper generalization of the generic point of a component: the closure of any such generalization is irreducible and contains that maximal component, so equals it, and uniqueness of its generic point forces equality. Hence $f(x)=\eta$ and discreteness forces $x=\xi_i$. Each $\xi_i$ lies in an irreducible component of $X_0$; its generic point exists by sobriety, is a generalization of $\xi_i$, and therefore equals $\xi_i$. Distinct $\xi_i$ belong to distinct components.

If $n>0$, apply the affine-neighbourhood theorem to $X_0$, the finitely many components just obtained, and $x=\xi_1$. This gives an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}S\subseteq X_0$ containing the entire fibre over $\eta$. If $n=0$, use the empty affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}(0)$. In both cases $U$ is affine and contains every point over $\eta$.

source.place: Tag 02NW, proof of (1) => (3); Properties Tag 01ZX (lemma-point-and-maximal-points-affine), refinement of 01ZV

proof.text: The affine-pairs finite-type criterion applied to $U\subseteq X$, $V_0\subseteq Y$ makes the induced map $\varphi:R\to S$ of finite type. The prime $\mathfrak p$ of $\eta$ is minimal by the spectrum/component correspondence: $\overline{\{\mathfrak p\}}=V(\mathfrak p)$, so a strictly smaller prime would contradict maximality of that component. The primes of $S$ contracting to $\mathfrak p$ are precisely the points of $U$ mapping to $\eta$, hence form a finite set. Apply the algebraic localization lemma to obtain $g\notin\mathfrak p$ with $R_g\to S_{\varphi(g)}$ finite. Put $V_1=D(g)\subseteq V_0$ and $U_1=U\cap f^{-1}(V_1)=D(\varphi(g))$. The basic-open pullback identity and principal-localization open immersion identify these with the affine schemes $\operatorname{Spec}R_g$ and $\operatorname{Spec}S_{\varphi(g)}$. Their induced ring map sends $a/g^k$ to $\varphi(a)/\varphi(g)^k$: it agrees with $\varphi$ on $R$ and preserves inverses of the now invertible $g$. Thus it is exactly the finite localized map just obtained. The affine-cover criterion for finite morphisms, applied to the one-member cover of $V_1$, shows $U_1\to V_1$ finite.

The closed subset $Z=X_0\setminus U$ has $\eta\notin f_0(Z)$ because $U$ contains the full fibre. By the closed-subset construction choose a closed immersion $i:T\to X_0$ with image $Z$, and put $j=f_0\circ i:T\to V_0$. This composite is quasi-compact: over any affine open $A\subseteq V_0$, its inverse image is homeomorphic to the closed subset $Z\cap f_0^{-1}(A)$ of the quasi-compact space $f_0^{-1}(A)$, hence is quasi-compact. If $\eta\in\overline{j(T)}$, the closure-specialization theorem gives $t\in T$ with $j(t)$ specializing to $\eta$. As proved in step 2, the component generic point $\eta$ has no proper generalization, so $j(t)=\eta$, contradicting $\eta\notin f_0(Z)$. Consequently $W=V_0\setminus\overline{j(T)}$ is open, contains $\eta$, and $f_0^{-1}(W)\cap Z=\varnothing$. Choose a principal open $V_\eta=D(h)$ of $V_0$ with $\eta\in V_\eta\subseteq W\cap V_1$. Then $f^{-1}(V_\eta)\subseteq U$, so it equals $U_1\cap f^{-1}(V_\eta)$ as an open subscheme. It is therefore the restriction of the finite morphism $U_1\to V_1$ to $V_\eta$, hence finite by target restriction.

source.place: Tag 02NW, proof of (3) => (4), complement removal; its generic-image argument is expanded using the existing closure-specialization theorem (Stacks Tag 02JQ).

proof.text: Perform the preceding construction for every generic point $\eta$ and set $V=\bigcup_\eta V_\eta$. Each $V_\eta$ is an affine open of $Y$, hence of $V$, and these opens cover $V$. The finite-local-on-target lemma shows $f^{-1}(V)\to V$ finite. The union contains every component generic point. For any $y\in Y$, choose an irreducible component containing $y$ and its generic point $\eta$. Since $\eta\in V$ and $y\in\overline{\{\eta\}}$, one has $y\in\overline V$, so $V$ is dense. If $Y$ is empty, take $V=\varnothing$; the same cover criterion is vacuous and its preimage is empty. No intersection of the different $V_\eta$ is taken, since such an intersection could lose other generic points.
